subtopic: Caffeine, nicotine, alcohol and other substances
passage:
The farewell party in the Pune flat ran late, rain was hammering down, and the last bus had gone. A few drinks in, Jatin felt brilliant: funnier, louder, sure everyone loved his jokes. When Parul laughed at one, he read it as interest and kept draping his arm round her shoulders, even after she shifted away twice. Then he announced he'd ride his scooter home in the rain. "I'm totally fine." It sounded completely reasonable to him.
His friend Samar took the keys. "Not tonight. You're sleeping on my sofa."
In the grey morning, head pounding, Jatin replayed the evening. Parul hadn't been flirting; she'd been polite, and he had made her uncomfortable. And the scooter, in that rain. His stomach turned. He messaged her: "I'm sorry about last night. I crossed a line."

qa.a: His friend Samar took the keys.

qa.q: How did Jatin feel while drinking?
qa.a: Jatin felt brilliant and bold, sure everyone loved his jokes.

qa.q: What was the wise step at the party, and what did Jatin do the next morning?
qa.a: Samar took the keys so Jatin wouldn't ride in the rain; the next morning Jatin admitted crossing a line and apologised to Parul.

qa.q: How did the evening feel for Parul?
qa.a: Parul was uncomfortable, shifting away twice while Jatin misread her politeness as interest.

grounding: A young person who has been drinking feels bolder, misreads someone's politeness and plans a risky ride that seems reasonable at the time.

passage:
At his cousin's sangeet on a Jaipur rooftop, Yash had been drinking steadily since eight. The music was loud and everything felt easy. When a friend joked that no one could climb the water-tank ladder in the dark, Yash was already pulling off his jacket. "Watch me." The ladder was wet from the evening wash. In the moment, it seemed a perfectly sensible idea.
His cousin Sarika grabbed his arm. "Yash. Look at me. You can't even walk straight."
"I'm fine!" he said, too loudly, and swayed.
Sarika didn't argue further. She steered him to a chair, pushed a glass of water into his hand and stayed beside him. Much later, clearer-headed, he looked at the slick, rusty ladder and went pale. "Why did that seem like a good idea?"

qa.q: What did a friend joke that no one could climb?
qa.a: The water-tank ladder in the dark.

qa.q: How did Yash feel when he looked at the ladder later?
qa.a: Yash felt shaken and shocked, going pale and wondering why it had seemed a good idea.

qa.q: Which of Sarika's choices kept Yash safe?
qa.a: Sarika grabbed his arm, didn't argue further, sat him down with water and stayed beside him.

qa.q: How might Sarika have felt watching Yash pull off his jacket?
qa.a: Sarika was probably alarmed, seeing that Yash couldn't walk straight and was heading for a wet ladder.

grounding: Drinking makes a young person bolder and less careful, so a dangerous dare feels reasonable in the moment.
